# SolarWinds Orion Guides

> Documentation, schema, and automation reference for SolarWinds Orion, now sold as
> SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted. The schema is shipped as machine-readable JSON
> extracted from SolarWinds' own published sources, so an answer can be grounded in a
> lookup rather than recalled.

Read AGENTS.md first. It states the one rule that matters here: never state a schema fact
you have not looked up, because entity names, property names and verb parameter order are
the things models get plausibly but subtly wrong. AGENTS.md also carries the full list of
facts you can state without looking anything up.

Everything below works offline. No server, no network, no credentials.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how an AI system should use this repository, and the commands to look things up
- [README.md](README.md): what the repository is and how it is built
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): the verification discipline this repository is held to

If you are new to the platform's API, read [docs/swis/README.md](docs/swis/README.md) then
[docs/swql/README.md](docs/swql/README.md), in that order. If you are here to look
something up, jump to [docs/reference/](docs/reference/README.md).

## Look something up

- `python3 tools/schema_query.py find <keyword> --properties`: which entity holds this
- `python3 tools/schema_query.py show <Entity>`: properties, relationships, verbs, access control
- `python3 tools/schema_query.py verb <Entity> <Verb>`: parameters in order, required right, call syntax
- `python3 tools/schema_query.py path <From> <To>`: how to join A to B
- `python3 tools/validate_swql.py -`: check a query against the schema before using it

## Machine-readable data (platform version 2026.2)

- [data/schema/2026.2/index.json](data/schema/2026.2/index.json): 2067 entities, one compact record each
- [data/schema/2026.2/entities/](data/schema/2026.2/entities/): full records with 19,328 properties
- [data/schema/2026.2/verbs.json](data/schema/2026.2/verbs.json): 1021 verbs, 848 with typed ordered parameters
- [data/schema/2026.2/relationships.json](data/schema/2026.2/relationships.json): 2992 navigation edges
- [data/schema/2026.2/types.json](data/schema/2026.2/types.json): the shape of what 542 verbs return, and the enums their members use
- [data/reference/swql-functions.json](data/reference/swql-functions.json): function signatures and examples
- [data/reference/status-codes.json](data/reference/status-codes.json): status id to name, rank, meaning
- [data/reference/netobject-types.json](data/reference/netobject-types.json): NetObject prefixes and key properties
- [data/reference/reconciliation.json](data/reference/reconciliation.json): where sources disagree, and entity renames

## Working examples

Runnable code lives outside `docs/`:

- [scripts/swql/](scripts/swql/): 207 sample queries, all validated against the schema
- [scripts/powershell/](scripts/powershell/), [scripts/python/](scripts/python/) and
  [scripts/curl/](scripts/curl/) cover the three clients
- [tools/](tools/README.md) explores the schema offline and validates SWQL

## Where this repository is uncertain

[docs/reference/unverified.md](docs/reference/unverified.md) collects every statement the
guides decline to assert, gathered from the pages themselves so it cannot drift from them.
It covers what the schema does not record: behaviour only a running server exhibits,
values that are installation data rather than schema, and places where SolarWinds' own
documentation and their published contract disagree. Read it before answering something
load-bearing from this repository alone, and when a question lands on one of those points,
say it is unverified here and give the `Metadata.*` query that settles it.

## When this repository is not the authority

It documents one platform version, and the schema varies with the release and with which
modules are licensed. For a specific server, ask that server through the `Metadata.*`
entities: see [docs/swis/metadata-introspection.md](docs/swis/metadata-introspection.md)
and [scripts/swql/08-schema-introspection.swql](scripts/swql/08-schema-introspection.swql).

Upgrading between versions: [docs/reference/](docs/reference/README.md) carries generated
change reports that classify each difference by risk, and the class worth knowing about is
a verb whose positional arguments shifted, because an existing call still has the right
number of arguments and sends them into the wrong slots.

## A note on trust

Every entity, property, verb and parameter named in these pages was checked against the
extracted schema before it was written, and every SWQL example is re-validated on each
build. Where a claim could not be verified, it says so rather than asserting quietly.

The version documented here is **2026.2**. The schema changes between releases and also
depends on which modules are licensed, so for a specific server the authority is that
server: see [docs/swis/metadata-introspection.md](docs/swis/metadata-introspection.md).
